title: SDK Hackathon 30m Demo Kit — zero-to-hello
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, highly opinionated 30-minute kit meant for internal hackathons, office hours, and demo booths. The goal: get a developer from zero to a reproducible "hello+LLM" demo, with a minimal smoke harness and a few rapid recovery knobs. Focus is on reliability and repeatability rather than feature completeness.

Target audience:
- Engineers who want to demo Redwood SDKs quickly
- Developer advocates running workshops
- New hires doing a 30-minute product walkthrough

Success criteria (30 min):
- Install and run sample app locally (10 min)
- Make 3 successful API calls (generation, chat, embeddings) (7 min)
- Run smoke script that validates responses and basic telemetry (5 min)
- Show fallback behavior (fallback model or cached response) (5 min)
- Capture a short gif/screencap (3 min)

Prep (5–10 min before):
- Ensure dev laptop has: node >=18, npm/yarn, git, docker optional
- Pre-create demo API key (hosted) or point to local mock token
- Clone lightweight template repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-templates (branch: hackathon-30m)
- Create a single-slide README for the booth with exact commands (we'll keep this in the repo)

Kickoff checklist (step-by-step):
1) Clone and install (2–3 min)
   git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-templates.git && cd sdk-templates/hackathon-30m
   npm install  # or yarn

2) Configure credentials (1 min)
   # Option A: hosted (recommended for demos)
   export REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood_demo_KEY_XXXX

   # Option B: local run (if offline)
   ./scripts/start-local-mock.sh  # starts a tiny mock server on :8080 and prints MOCK_KEY
   export REDWOOD_API_URL=http://localhost:8080 && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=MOCK_KEY

3) Run quick start server (1 min)
   npm run dev  # lightweight express app listens on 3000 and exposes /generate /chat /embed endpoints

4) Make sample calls (curl) (2–3 min)
   # generation
   curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:3000/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"Hello from hackathon"}'

   # chat
   curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:3000/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize this repo in one sentence"}]}'

   # embeddings
   curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:3000/embed -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"input":"Redwood inference demo"}'

5) Run smoke harness (2 min)
   # smoke script checks status codes, simple regex on text and logs a tiny telemetry event
   ./scripts/smoke.sh
   # Expected output (3 checks): generation contains "Hello", chat contains "Summarize", embeddings vector length > 0

6) Show graceful fallback (2–5 min)
   # Toggle a simulated outage
   curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/_simulate/outage  # if using mock
   # Trigger route that falls back to cached response or a smaller model
   curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/generate -d '{"prompt":"Hello from hackathon"}'
   # Demo notes: explain routing policy and canary fallback (talk track in slide)

Quick talking points (for demos):
- We prioritize predictable latency for demoers: default template uses a small quantized open model for quick response (low tokens, low cost).
- SDK provides the same API shape for hosted/dedicated/private — we change only environment variables.
- Telemetry is lightweight in template: success/failure counters + token counts. Show console events.

Lightweight telemetry knobs (explain):
- Telemetry enabled via REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=1 (default for hackathon)
- smoke.sh records: request_id, model_variant, latency_ms, tokens_sent
- privacy note: demo key logs are ephemeral and scrubbed after event

Files of interest in template repo (one-liners):
- README-hackathon.md  — exact commands + booth cheat sheet
- server.js  — tiny express wrapper for SDK calls and simple HTML playground
- scripts/smoke.sh  — minimal assertions and exit codes for CI/demo gating
- scripts/start-local-mock.sh — very small mock that simulates latency, error rates, and fallback behavior
- templates/demo-prompt.txt — recommended prompts for engaging Q/A

Smoke script internals (for maintainers):
- Uses curl + jq to assert 200 response and presence of token_count in json
- Exit code 0 if all checks pass, 1 otherwise
- Sleep/backoff strategy between retries is conservative (3 attempts, 400ms backoff)

What to capture for a good demo clip (30–60s):
- Start server, make one generate and one chat call, show the smoke.sh passing, then simulate outage and show fallback responding.
- Save with asciinema or short screencast; store link in a shared sheet.

Risks & quick mitigations:
- Rate limit surprises on hosted demo keys: limit attendees to sequential demos, or use local mock for large groups.
- Network flakiness: have a fallback wifi hotspot and local mock available.
- Unexpected breaking changes in SDK: pin SDK version in package.json and vendor dist in repo if needed.

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Should the template include a tiny Web UI with streaming to show progressive tokens? Pros: nicer demos. Cons: adds fragility. (DECIDE: next sprint)
- Do we want a single demo key per booth or user-specific keys for telemetry? (security ask: product ops)
- Add a small test that asserts streaming chunk ordering for basic streaming demos. (owner: Priya)

Post-demo housekeeping (2 min):
- Revoke demo API key if used hosted (security runbook)
- Clear mock state: ./scripts/reset-mock.sh
- Paste any interesting logs to #dx-hackathon for follow-ups

Notes to self (Maya):
- Keep template < 100 LOC in server.js and Make smoke.sh super forgiving — people hate fiddly CI failures at booths.
- Consider adding a `--no-telemetry` flag for privacy-conscious partners.

Related artifacts / reading (internal):
- Hacks: repo branch hackathon-30m contains starter slide and GIF export script
- See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-templates/pull/312 for latest changes

If you run this at a booth — ping me in slack @maya with time and I'll drop a small blurb and a pre-made image for the demo stand.
